title: Restore real-world 2D drafting foundation from CAD-BENCH-RW-001
objective: Restore a trustworthy 2D drafting foundation on current mainline, beginning with canonical document/layer/selection state integrity exposed by the CAD-BENCH-RW-001 production black-box benchmark, without changing frozen Architecture v1.1 or Construction Graph authority.
acceptance_criteria: UI-created and command-created layers resolve to one canonical document layer table and active-layer changes cause newly created entities to use the selected canonical layer.
NEW fully resets document/editor state, including active-layer references, selection, transient command state, view state and entity-count state, with no dangling references or phantom entities.
Command selection, canvas picking and Properties selection share one canonical selection state and screen-space picking uses a deterministic declared tolerance.
Successful command feedback is emitted only after the canonical transaction commits; failed operations expose explicit typed failure without a preceding false success claim.

The golden browser workflows G1, G2, G3, G5, G7, G8, G9 and G10 from CAD-BENCH-RW-001 have reproducible before/after evidence showing the targeted foundation defects are resolved or honestly typed where outside this slice.
Deterministic automated tests cover layer identity/activation, NEW reset, selection synchronization, screen-space picking tolerance, entity-count integrity and authoritative command feedback.
Web and Electron preserve the same affected semantic behavior through the shared App API and existing engine/adapter boundaries remain unchanged.
Existing verified CAD/BIM regression baselines remain green and the change introduces no architecture drift or protected-path modification without an ACR.
non_goals: No HATCH feature implementation in this slice.
No new BIM authoring scope beyond what is unlocked by the repaired selection foundation.
No architecture modification; Architecture v1.1 remains frozen.
No self-approval or self-verification by the implementation agent.
risk_assumptions: CAD-BENCH-RW-001 is the current black-box observation of main and its findings supersede historical assumptions that COMPAT-CAD-001 behavior remains present.
Historical COMPAT-CAD-001 Issue #37 / PR #38 is not reused as current-state evidence because mainline behavior has diverged since that merge.
The layer/selection failures appear to share canonical-identity/state synchronization roots; implementation must prove this rather than patch individual UI symptoms.
Viewport clipping, zoom/pan and ARRAY materialization are deliberately deferred until the first state/selection slice is stable.

The selection semantic deliberately changed from 'survives undo/redo' to 'pruned to live elements' (CADDocument.execute/undo/redo + setSelection filtering): the benchmark proved the unfiltered store produces the Sel-1/No-selection desync (DEF-008) and phantom counts (DEF-014); the re-pinned test documents the change in-code.

The plan outcome echoes are deferred through the shared splitEchoTiming invariant (output lines always end with the plan echo block) rather than editing the command registry — zero drift for the pinned certification corpora, identical semantics on both hosts.

PICKBOX_SCREEN_PX = 10 (AutoCAD's default pickbox) declared in the shared precision module and converted through the view transform at every pick site; the DEF-006 root cause (the command line reflowing the canvas under the cursor) is fixed by the fixed-height command-line panel, not by inflating the tolerance.
Snapshot adoption uses a version-monotonic guard (a late response can never roll the client back); document.create/open adoptions are the intentional reset path and bypass the guard.

Viewport partial clipping (DEF-004), zoom/pan vocabulary (DEF-005), ARRAY materialization (DEF-015) and durable persistence (DEF-009) remain the documented second slice; the serverless multi-instance session divergence is acknowledged as the persistence/session-identity problem, out of this slice.

Pre-existing main-side defect disclosure: governance/work-items/CAD-PARITY-020.json lost the schema-required 'dependencies' field at main commit 3090846, which crashes validateRepository (TypeError: record.dependencies is not iterable) and has kept the governance workflow red on every main commit since 2026-09-04T02:01:57Z. This defect and ALL remaining CAD-PARITY-020 ledger defects (the missing registry field, the transition-reference schema violations, the EV-003 evidence type, the MERGED->VERIFIED decision reference, the DEC-002 re-verification-policy violations) are Architect authority — the record is VERIFIED and its repair is not implementation-agent scope. An earlier revision of this PR had restored the 'dependencies' field byte-exact (08e77e-era value ['CAD-PARITY-019']) to convert the crash into the designed attributable-failure mode; the Architect's CHANGES REQUIRED review of PR #137 (comment 5547626071) ruled that modification of a VERIFIED record outside the implementation agent's scope, and it has been reverted byte-exact to main at f6d8d36: the VERIFIED record is again identical to main, the validate.ts crash returns to being the disclosed pre-existing main-side condition (identical to clean main, PR #133 precedent), and the P020 repair remains with the Architect — disclosed, not touched, not fixed by this PR.
evidence_requirements: Deterministic tests for canonical layer identity, active-layer behavior, NEW reset and entity-count integrity.
Deterministic tests and real-browser evidence for unified selection state and screen-space object picking.
Tests proving failed canonical transactions do not emit false success feedback.
Web/Electron parity evidence for affected semantics.
Exact-head CI evidence with existing CAD/BIM regressions remaining green.
Production or exact preview browser evidence rerunning the targeted CAD-BENCH-RW-001 golden workflows.
Evidence that Architecture v1.1, Construction Graph authority and engine/worker boundaries remain intact.

transitions.reason: CAD-BENCH-RW-001 production benchmark identified systemic drafting foundation failures; the remediation scope is bounded to current requirement CAD-001 and frozen Architecture v1.1.
Architect release directive: z-ai-implementation-agent is authorized to implement COMPAT-CAD-005 from verified mainline and must stop at PR_OPEN/VERIFYING.

Begin the first foundation slice from main 311815f: layer identity unification via authoritative snapshot adoption, NEW full editor reset, unified/pruned selection state, declared screen-space pick tolerance with a stable viewport, and commit-authoritative command echo.

First foundation slice implemented and PR #137 opened at implementation head f10162f2: canonical layer identity via authoritative response-snapshot adoption, NEW full editor reset, unified live-pruned selection, declared 10 px screen-space pickbox with a stable fixed-height command-line viewport, and commit-authoritative echo timing on both hosts.

Evidence package attached; implementation agent stopped at VERIFYING. The later Architect CHANGES REQUIRED decision on review head 946872d ruled the one-line mutation of VERIFIED CAD-PARITY-020 out of scope; that mutation was reverted byte-exact at f6d8d36, exact-head evidence was rerun, and the remediation head is bd9a4ab. No self-approval or self-verification.

Independent Architect re-review of the remediation head bd9a4ab confirms the forbidden CAD-PARITY-020 mutation is absent, the remaining 18-file change set is within COMPAT-CAD-005 scope, Architecture v1.1 remains frozen, exact-head local and CI evidence is terminal with only the byte-identical pre-existing main governance failure, and the exact-head preview/browser verification satisfies the first-slice acceptance contract with serverless multi-instance divergence explicitly disclosed.

DEC-003 authorizes merge. The remediation fully satisfies the prior CHANGES REQUIRED decision: the VERIFIED predecessor record is untouched, exact-head evidence is revision-bound, no protected architecture path changed, and the first-slice acceptance criteria are supported. GitHub's formal APPROVE endpoint rejected the attempt because the connected account is the PR author, so this canonical governance decision is recorded here rather than represented as a platform review by a different identity. Post-merge verification remains mandatory and separate.
